findings.detail: CHANGELOG.md line 5 adds `darkbloom cache set --directory ...`, which moves encrypted SSD prefix-cache files to an operator-chosen external volume, and pins the volume UUID. T-041 assumes a single on-box root (darkbloom/kv3). It also assumes the 30-minute sliding TTL, the opportunistic sweep and the disk budget bound how long DBK3 artifacts exist. If the external disk is unmounted or replaced, the provider 'refuses ... without falling back', so the sweep cannot run. Encrypted files then persist on a removable, portable device well past the TTL. The HMAC-named files also keep leaking file count, sizes and mtimes. The KEK stays on the Mac, which limits content exposure; the KEK wipe remains the crypto purge. The threat model does not cover this new at-rest location, the TTL-expiry gap for detached media, or the trust placed in the volume UUID and 'encryption required' check. Update T-041 and TB-007 to cover external roots. State that TTL and LRU purge need the volume mounted, and that the KEK wipe is the only purge for detached media. Confirm the encryption check cannot be bypassed by a user-controlled mount.
findings.title: External prefix-cache volume option changes the T-041 at-rest threat model (TTL purge, volume trust)

findings.detail: The new section lets operators point the encrypted prefix cache at an arbitrary directory, including an external or removable SSD. It also says that after a location switch the old ciphertext is never swept or securely erased. T-041 and its mitigations (SSD at-rest window bounded by a 30-minute sliding TTL and an available-disk/2 LRU budget, 20 GiB reserve, KEK wipe as purge) assume one on-box store that maintenance fully controls. After a switch, or if the operator keeps a detachable disk, stale DBK3 files persist indefinitely. Their file sizes, timestamps, model and layout binding, and HMAC tags stay observable to an adversarial provider operator or whoever holds the disk. The doc also admits that a malicious controller can retain ciphertext, replay still-valid ciphertext, or defeat the filesystem-UUID pin by cloning it. The result is a new at-rest surface (removable or untrusted peripherals) and a new replay and rollback surface that T-041, T-016 and TB-003 do not cover. Their disk-budget, TTL and purge mitigations are also silent on which volume they apply to. Fix: update T-041 and TB-003 to cover a configurable payload location, orphaned ciphertext after a switch, and external-controller replay/retention. Consider sweeping or TTL-purging the previous directory on a switch, binding the freshness or TTL check to a Mac-local ledger, and scoping the budget and reserve to the selected volume.
findings.title: Relocatable cache directory breaks the TTL-bounded at-rest claim in the threat model
